prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The 2001 Conservative Party manifesto, “Time for Common Sense,” pledges to shift power from government to people, strengthen national institutions, and apply “common sense” across public services, the economy, and national life.

- Families and education: Cut taxes for families (raise Children’s Tax Credit for under-5s; new Married Couple’s Allowance via transferable personal allowance; remove tax on widowed parents’ allowances). Reform Working Families Tax Credit to be paid to the caring parent. Create Family Scholarships for parents returning to work. Establish “Free Schools” with autonomy for heads/governors; curb exclusions bureaucracy; set up Progress Centres for disruptive pupils; let successful schools expand; allow new faith/parent/company schools; give parents power to trigger Ofsted and force leadership change. No top-up fees; raise student loan repayment threshold to £20,000. Endow universities for independence.

- Crime and justice: Increase police numbers; cut red tape (“cops in shops,” parish constables). Tougher action on persistent young offenders (10x more Secure Training Centre places, minimum 6 months linked to behaviour/qualifications). Mandatory jail for dealers selling to under-16s; tougher penalties near schools. “Honesty in sentencing” (end automatic/special early release); prison work to fund victim reparations/families. Lifetime supervision options for sex offenders; protect children online. Victims get named contacts in police/CPS; reform self-defence and double jeopardy.

- Economy and tax: Keep the pound; enhance BoE MPC independence; spending growth within trend. Deliver £8bn annual tax cuts funded by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence: abolish taxes on most savings/dividends; raise pensioners’ personal allowance by £2,000; new Married Couple’s Allowance; cut petrol duty by at least 6p; business tax reliefs; abolish IR35. Simpler, more transparent taxes; independent National Accounts Commission. Slash regulation via a Deregulation Commission and departmental “regulatory budgets”; small-business exemptions. Scrap Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear; boost competition in utilities.

- NHS: Match Labour spending but end politicised targets. Replace Waiting List Initiative with a Patient’s Guarantee (maximum waits by clinical need, choice of NHS/other hospitals). Restore ward sisters/matrons’ authority. GP/patient choice of hospital; allow proven complementary therapies. Remove tax penalties on employer-provided private cover when affordable. Fund hospices better; expand surgical units and practice nurses; Exceptional Medicines Fund for high-cost drugs.

- Older people and pensions: Abolish most taxes on savings; raise age-related allowance by £2,000 (remove 1m pensioners from tax). Increase basic state pension, with extra for over-75s; optional consolidation of winter fuel/TV licence into higher tax-free pension. Offer funded pension option for younger workers; abolish compulsory annuity at 75; protect assets for long-term care; free nursing care at point of use.

- Europe, defence, and asylum: In Europe but not run by it—keep pound; veto further power transfers; renegotiate Nice; “reserved powers” in UK law; stronger single market/competition; curb EU waste. Back NATO; oppose EU army outside NATO; support missile defence; meet full manning; exempt forces from ECHR. Aid focused on good governance; double share via charities; pursue transatlantic FTA and global free trade by 2020. Fix asylum with secure reception centres, safe-country rules, and a Removals Agency.

- Welfare and civil society: Office of Civil Society; abolish irrecoverable VAT for charities (funded from euro-prep budgets). Replace New Deal with “Britain Works” paying providers for sustained jobs; Can Work, Must Work. Require lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work. Improve disabled savings rules; new incapacity agency focused on rehab. National anti-fraud squad; clean up NI numbers.

- Town, country, transport, environment: Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; honest food labelling; cut red tape. Support rural services (business rate cuts, benefit card via post offices, transport fuel rebates); cut fuel duty 6p; abolish top-down housebuilding targets; protect “Blue Belts.” Urban revival via Regeneration Companies, extra policing, Partner Schools, brownfield-first planning, stronger Right to Buy, rent-to-mortgage, homesteading grants. Transport: invest in roads/public transport; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; Brit Disc for foreign lorries; rail safety reforms. Climate policy via trading, efficiency, renewables, cleaner generation.

- Culture/media/sport: Privatise Channel 4; create £3bn endowment for arts from sale and Lottery surpluses; restore Lottery independence; boost tourism promotion. Protect school sport/playfields; charitable status for local clubs; streamline sport quangos. Single communications regulator; liberalise ownership; fair BBC oversight; equal access for religious broadcasters.

- Democracy: Empower top-performing “free councils”; local referendums for big council tax rises; retain Section 28. Scrap RDAs/Regional Assemblies; devolve enterprise to counties/unitaries. English Votes for English Laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and a substantial elected element; PM to face Commons twice weekly; stronger select committees; keep FPTP. Cut ministers, MPs (after scrutiny reforms), and spin doctors. Maintain NI within UK; implement Belfast Agreement with decommissioning and robust security.
